Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

particular adjective

specific, this and not another

also specific, in particular, particularly, especially

classical

Ov. Rem. 189: temporibus certīs
Varr. RR 2.1.19: certō tempore

certus, certa, certum

particular, fixed, specified

Particular as against any at all: certīs diēbus, on particular days; “this particular …” is often ipse: hōc ipsō diē.

Other words

  • praecipuē — in particular, especially, above all

    adverb · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 7.1: quid tibi vītandum praecipuē exīstimēs quaeris? turbam; Hor. Ep. 1.1.108: praecipuē sānus, nisi cum pītuīta molesta est

  • praesertim — particularly, especially (adding a weighty reason)

    adverb; most often with cum or sī · also used · classical · Varr. RR 3.2.3: tē praesertim

    Traupman gives potissimum, “above all”, for “in particular” (p. 356).

  • particulāris, particulāre — of a part, partial; in logic, particular

    avoid · post-classical · Apul. Dogm. Plat. 3 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 356

    Traupman’s word for “particular”, but post-classical and a term of logic (prōpositiōnēs particulārēs, opposed to universal ones); certus and praecipuus say it classically.

Examples

  • quid tibi vītandum praecipuē exīstimēs quaeris? turbam

    you ask what I think you should avoid in particular? CrowdsSen. Ep. 7.1

  • dextera praecipuē capit indulgentia mentēs

    it is kindness, in particular, that wins heartsOv. Ars 2.145

  • temporibus certīs mātūram rūsticus ūvam dēligit

    at particular times the farmer picks the ripe grapesOv. Rem. 189–190

See also particular, individual.
